subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes along a Lipschitz graph
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), W ⊆ U open, ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, a ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, L ≥ 0 and f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ L-Lipschitz. Then for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ M ∩ W (μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ W)-a.e.): for every v ∈ ℝⁿ with x = a + ιv + ι'(f(v)), f is differentiable at v and approxTangentPlane n M x = LinearMap.range(ι + ι'∘Df(v)) = {ιw + ι'Df(v)w : w ∈ ℝⁿ}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (U W : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (R : IMRep U n) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (a : Euclid (n + k)) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (L : NNReal), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → LipschitzWith L f → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ W)), ∀ v : Euclid n, x = a + ι v + ι' (f v) → DifferentiableAt ℝ f v ∧ approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x = LinearMap.range (ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (fderiv ℝ f v).toLinearMap)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Part 1.6 (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(2) and the proof of 1.6; Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2); Ch. 2, 3.5). Conventions: E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_λ(x) closed ball, Bⁿ_λ(v) closed ball of ℝⁿ; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, Hⁿ := μHE[n] (equal to Lebesgue measure Lⁿ on ℝⁿ and on every n-plane), ω_n := unitBallVolume n. For x, λ > 0, η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^{−1}(y − x) (library blowUpMap), so Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(A)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(A). "M has approximate tangent plane P at x" means HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P: dim P = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)}ψ dHⁿ → ∫_P ψ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported ψ : E → ℝ.

0. Setup. Let Φ(v) := a + ιv + ι'(f v) (v ∈ ℝⁿ) and F := Φ(ℝⁿ). Since ι, ι' are linear isometries with orthogonal ranges, |Φ(v₁) − Φ(v₂)|² = |v₁ − v₂|² + |f(v₁) − f(v₂)|²; hence Φ is injective, Lipschitz with constant (1 + L²)^{1/2}, and |v₁ − v₂| ≤ |Φ(v₁) − Φ(v₂)|. For each x ∈ F there is exactly one v with x = Φ(v). For v where f is differentiable let P_v := LinearMap.range(ι + ι'∘Df(v)) = {ιw + ι'Df(v)w : w ∈ ℝⁿ}, an n-plane (w ↦ ιw + ι'Df(v)w is injective), and J(v) := (det(I + Df(v)ᵀDf(v)))^{1/2} ∈ [1, (1 + L²)^{n/2}], the area Jacobian of Φ at v; A ↦ (det(I + AᵀA))^{1/2} is smooth, hence Lipschitz on {‖A‖ ≤ L}.
1. Good parameters. By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) f is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. v; Df (defined a.e.) is bounded and measurable, so by Lebesgue's differentiation theorem Lⁿ-a.e. v is a Lebesgue point of Df: λ^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_λ(v)}|Df(v') − Df(v)|dv' → 0. Let N be the Lⁿ-null set of v at which one of these fails. Since Φ is Lipschitz, Hⁿ(Φ(N)) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2}Hⁿ(N) = 0 (Mathlib LipschitzWith/LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le).
2. F has approximate tangent plane P_v at x = Φ(v) for v ∉ N. Let ψ be continuous with spt ψ ⊆ B_{R'}(0), and λ > 0. Since F ∩ K ⊆ Φ(Bⁿ_m(0)) for every compact K and large m, Hⁿ(F ∩ K) < ∞, so ψ is integrable for Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(F) and the Bochner integrals in the library definition of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt are genuine integrals. Write ψ = ψ⁺ − ψ⁻ with ψ^± := max{±ψ, 0} continuous, nonnegative and supported in B_{R'}(0); the identities below are first obtained for ψ^± (the library area formulas are lower-integral statements with nonnegative weights) and then subtracted, all terms being finite. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5–3.7; library injective_area_formula_lipschitz / weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn) and the scaling of Hⁿ, ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)}ψ dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_F ψ(η_{x,λ}(y))dHⁿ(y) = λ^{−n}∫_{ℝⁿ}ψ((Φ(v') − x)/λ)J(v')dv' = ∫_{ℝⁿ}ψ(ιw + ι'f_λ(w))J(v + λw)dw, where f_λ(w) := (f(v + λw) − f(v))/λ (substitution v' = v + λw). As |ιw + ι'f_λ(w)| ≥ |w|, the integrand vanishes for |w| > R', and it is bounded by sup|ψ|(1 + L²)^{n/2}. As λ ↓ 0: f_λ → Df(v) uniformly on Bⁿ_{R'}(0) (differentiability at v), so ψ(ιw + ι'f_λ(w)) → ψ(ιw + ι'Df(v)w) uniformly there (ψ is uniformly continuous); and ∫_{Bⁿ_{R'}(0)}|J(v + λw) − J(v)|dw = λ^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{λR'}(v)}|J − J(v)| ≤ Lip·λ^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{λR'}(v)}|Df − Df(v)| → 0 (Lebesgue point). Hence ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)}ψ dHⁿ → ∫_{ℝⁿ}ψ(ιw + ι'Df(v)w)J(v)dw = ∫_{P_v}ψ dHⁿ, the last equality by the area formula for the injective linear map w ↦ ιw + ι'Df(v)w, whose Jacobian is J(v). Thus HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n F x P_v.
3. Vanishing densities. Let A₁ := (M ∖ F) ∩ W and A₂ := F ∖ M; both are Borel (M is Borel, F = ∪_m Φ(Bⁿ_m(0)) is σ-compact). Write W = ∪_j V_j with V_j := {y ∈ W : |y| < j, dist(y, E ∖ W) > 1/j} (V_j := {|y| < j} if W = E); each V_j is open with compact closure in W. Each Borel set A_i ∩ V_j has finite Hⁿ-measure: for compact K ⊆ W, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M, IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult, K ⊆ U), and F ∩ K ⊆ Φ(Bⁿ_m(0)) for m ≥ sup_K|y − a|, whose Hⁿ-measure is ≤ (1+L²)^{n/2}ω_nmⁿ < ∞. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; library simon_theorem_3_6, applied to the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ and the Hⁿ-measurable set A_i ∩ V_j of finite measure), limsup_{λ↓0}Hⁿ(A_i ∩ V_j ∩ B_λ(x))/λⁿ = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A_i ∩ V_j (library glue: apply simon_theorem_3_6 to the Borel regular outer measure of Hⁿ⌞(A_i ∩ V_j) (measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular) and transfer the Simon-normalized null set to μHE[n] by simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; both have the same null sets). If x ∈ V_j then B_λ(x) ⊆ V_j for small λ, so limsup_{λ↓0}Hⁿ(A_i ∩ B_λ(x))/λⁿ = 0. Taking the (countable) union over j of the exceptional sets: the density of Hⁿ⌞A_i vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ W ∖ A_i (i = 1, 2), in particular at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, which is disjoint from A₁ ∪ A₂.
4. Transfer to M. Let x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, x = Φ(v), with v ∉ N and with both densities of 3 equal to 0 at x. For ψ as in 2 with spt ψ ⊆ B_{R'}(0) and λ small enough that B_{λR'}(x) ⊆ W (then Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λR'}(x)) < ∞, as θ ≥ 1 on M and IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult applies to the compact set B_{λR'}(x) ⊆ W ⊆ U, so both integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals): |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)}ψ dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)}ψ dHⁿ| ≤ sup|ψ|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ((M △ F) ∩ B_{λR'}(x)) ≤ sup|ψ|·λ^{−n}(Hⁿ(A₁ ∩ B_{λR'}(x)) + Hⁿ(A₂ ∩ B_{λR'}(x))) → 0. With 2, ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)}ψ dHⁿ → ∫_{P_v}ψ dHⁿ, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P_v. Therefore the existential condition in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds at x and, by uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), approxTangentPlane n M x = P_v = LinearMap.range(ι + ι'∘Df(v)); moreover f is differentiable at v since v ∉ N.
5. Conclusion. Let Z := Φ(N) ∪ Z₁ ∪ Z₂, where Z_i is the Hⁿ-null exceptional set of 3 for A_i; Hⁿ(Z) = 0. For x ∈ (M ∩ W) ∖ Z and any v with x = a + ιv + ι'(f v): x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, v is the unique parameter of x, v ∉ N (as x ∉ Φ(N)), and both densities vanish at x; by 4, f is differentiable at v and approxTangentPlane n M x = LinearMap.range(ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ Df(v)). For x ∉ F the implication is vacuous. Since Z is Hⁿ-null, the assertion holds for μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ W)-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Rademacher and Lebesgue differentiation: off an Lⁿ-null set N, f is differentiable with Lebesgue points of Df, and Hⁿ(Φ(N)) = 0.
By the area formula and blow-up, F = Φ(ℝⁿ) has approximate tangent plane range(ι + ι'Df(v)) at Φ(v) for v ∉ N.
The upper density theorem (localized to sets compactly inside W) shows that the densities of Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ F) and Hⁿ⌞(F ∖ M) vanish Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ F ∩ W.
Transfer the approximate tangent plane from F to M and conclude by uniqueness of approxTangentPlane.

Source: parent proof Part 6 (Simon Ch. 5, Lemma 3.1 and its proof; estimates 3.2–3.4) and the use made of them in Part 7, Steps 7–8 ((17'), (18'), (19')). Conventions: Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ (Lean Euclid n); B̆_ρ, B_ρ open/closed balls of ℝⁿ centred at 0 unless indicated; ω_n := Lⁿ(B̆₁) ∈ (0, ∞); for a Lipschitz function w, ∇w := the a.e. derivative (Lean fderiv ℝ w, a linear functional whose operator norm |∇w| is the Euclidean norm of the gradient), ∇w·∇ζ := Σ_i ∂_iw ∂_iζ (the Lean sum over EuclideanSpace.single i 1). A Lipschitz function on B̆_ρ belongs to W^{1,2}(B̆_ρ) and its weak gradient equals its a.e. gradient. "Harmonic on B̆_ρ" means C² (hence C^∞) with Δh = 0 there.

Part A (Harmonic approximation, Simon 3.1, normalized). Claim: for every ε' > 0 there is δ_A(n, ε') > 0 such that if B := B̆₁ and w ∈ W^{1,2}(B) satisfies ∫_B|∇w|² ≤ 1 and |∫_B ∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δ_A sup|∇ζ| for every ζ ∈ C¹_c(B), then there is a harmonic h on B with ∫_B|∇h|² ≤ 1 and ∫_B(h − w)² ≤ ε'.
A1. Suppose not. Then there are ε' > 0 and w_j ∈ W^{1,2}(B) (j = 1, 2, …) with ∫_B|∇w_j|² ≤ 1, |∫_B ∇w_j·∇ζ| ≤ j^{−1}sup|∇ζ| for all ζ ∈ C¹_c(B), and ∫_B(w_j − h)² > ε' for every harmonic h on B with ∫_B|∇h|² ≤ 1.
A2. Let λ_j := ω_n^{−1}∫_B w_j. By the Poincaré inequality on the ball (e.g. [GT01, (7.45)]), ∫_B|w_j − λ_j|² ≤ C(n)∫_B|∇w_j|² ≤ C(n). Thus (w_j − λ_j) is bounded in W^{1,2}(B), and by Rellich's compactness theorem and weak compactness of bounded sets in L²(B) a subsequence (not relabelled) satisfies w_j − λ_j → w in L²(B) and ∇w_j ⇀ ∇w weakly in L²(B; ℝⁿ), with w ∈ W^{1,2}(B) and ∫_B|∇w|² ≤ liminf ∫_B|∇w_j|² ≤ 1 (weak lower semicontinuity of the norm).
A3. For ζ ∈ C¹_c(B), ∇ζ ∈ L²(B), so ∫_B ∇w·∇ζ = lim_j ∫_B ∇w_j·∇ζ = 0 by A1. By Weyl's lemma, w (after modification on a null set) is harmonic on B.
A4. h_j := w + λ_j is harmonic with ∫_B|∇h_j|² = ∫_B|∇w|² ≤ 1, and ∫_B(w_j − h_j)² = ∫_B(w_j − λ_j − w)² → 0 < ε', contradicting A1 for large j.
Part B (Scaling). Let R₀ > 0 and w ∈ W^{1,2}(B̆_{R₀}) with R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇w|² ≤ 1 and |∫_{B̆_{R₀}}∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δ_A R₀ⁿ sup|∇ζ| for all ζ ∈ C¹_c(B̆_{R₀}). Put w₁(y) := R₀^{−1}w(R₀y). Then ∇w₁(y) = ∇w(R₀y), ∫_B|∇w₁|² = R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇w|² ≤ 1; for ζ₁ ∈ C¹_c(B) let ζ(x) := R₀ζ₁(x/R₀) ∈ C¹_c(B̆_{R₀}), so ∇ζ(x) = ∇ζ₁(x/R₀), sup|∇ζ| = sup|∇ζ₁| and ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}∇w·∇ζ = R₀ⁿ∫_B∇w₁·∇ζ₁; hence |∫_B∇w₁·∇ζ₁| ≤ δ_A sup|∇ζ₁|. Part A gives a harmonic h₁ on B; then h(x) := R₀h₁(x/R₀) is harmonic on B̆_{R₀} with R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇h|² ≤ 1 and ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}(h − w)² = R₀^{n+2}∫_B(h₁ − w₁)² ≤ ε'R₀^{n+2}.
Part C (Estimates for harmonic functions, Simon 3.2–3.4). Let h be harmonic on B̆_{R₀} with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇h|² ≤ R₀ⁿ and h ∈ L²(B̆_{R₀}).
C1. Mean value property: h(0) = (ω_nρⁿ)^{−1}∫_{B̆_ρ}h for 0 < ρ < R₀; letting ρ ↑ R₀ (h ∈ L¹(B̆_{R₀})), h(0) = (ω_nR₀ⁿ)^{−1}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}h, so by Cauchy–Schwarz |h(0)| ≤ ω_n^{−1/2}R₀^{−n/2}‖h‖_{L²(B̆_{R₀})}.
C2. Each ∂_ih is harmonic, so likewise ∇h(0) = (ω_nR₀ⁿ)^{−1}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}∇h and |∇h(0)| ≤ ω_n^{−1/2}R₀^{−n/2}‖∇h‖_{L²(B̆_{R₀})} ≤ ω_n^{−1/2}.
C3. For |y| ≤ 3R₀/4, B̆_{R₀/4}(y) ⊆ B̆_{R₀}, so by the mean value property |∂_ih(y)| ≤ (ω_n(R₀/4)ⁿ)^{−1/2}‖∇h‖_{L²(B̆_{R₀})} ≤ 2ⁿω_n^{−1/2}. For a harmonic u on B̆_ρ(x), |∇u(x)| ≤ (n/ρ)sup_{B̆_ρ(x)}|u| (apply the mean value property to ∂_ju and the divergence theorem). With u = ∂_ih, ρ = R₀/4 and |x| ≤ R₀/2: |D²h(x)| ≤ C₁/R₀ for |x| ≤ R₀/2, C₁ := n^{3/2}·4·2ⁿω_n^{−1/2} (|D²h| the Hilbert–Schmidt norm).
C4. Let ℓ(v) := h(0) + ∇h(0)·v and θ' ∈ (0, 1/4]. For |v| ≤ θ'R₀ ≤ R₀/4, Taylor's formula with the segment [0, v] ⊆ B_{R₀/2} gives |h(v) − ℓ(v)| ≤ ½|v|² sup_{B_{R₀/2}}|D²h| ≤ ½C₁θ'²R₀.
Part D (Conclusion; Simon 3.4 and the computation (17')–(19') of the parent proof). Put C := max{ω_n^{−1/2}, 2, ½ω_nC₁²} (depends only on n) and, given ε' > 0, δ_h := δ_A(n, ε'). Let R₀ > 0 and w : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Lipschitz with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇w|² ≤ R₀ⁿ and |∫_{B̆_{R₀}}∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δ_h R₀ⁿ G whenever ζ is C¹ with compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ B̆_{R₀}, and |∇ζ| ≤ G everywhere (in particular with G = sup|∇ζ|). (Integrability: fderiv ℝ w is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv, valid for every function), and since w is Lipschitz with constant Lw, ‖fderiv ℝ w v‖ ≤ Lw for every v (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; fderiv is 0 where w is not differentiable); by Rademacher's theorem w is differentiable a.e., and, as recalled in the conventions, its a.e. derivative fderiv ℝ w is the weak gradient ∇w. For ζ as above, fderiv ℝ ζ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded. So the integrands ‖fderiv ℝ w v‖² and Σ_i ∂_iw(v)∂_iζ(v) of the two Lean hypotheses are bounded Borel functions on the ball B̆_{R₀}, which has finite measure, and their Bochner integrals are the Lebesgue integrals written here; likewise w² and (w − a − b)² are continuous, hence bounded on bounded balls, so the Bochner integrals in the conclusions are genuine Lebesgue integrals.) Then w|_{B̆_{R₀}} ∈ W^{1,2}(B̆_{R₀}) and Part B provides a harmonic h on B̆_{R₀} with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}|∇h|² ≤ R₀ⁿ and ∫_{B̆_{R₀}}(h − w)² ≤ ε'R₀^{n+2}; in particular h ∈ L²(B̆_{R₀}) (w is bounded on B̆_{R₀}). Let a := h(0) and b := Dh(0) (the linear functional v ↦ ∇h(0)·v; ‖b‖ = |∇h(0)|).
D1. ‖b‖ ≤ ω_n^{−1/2} ≤ C by C2.
D2. By C1 and Minkowski, |a| ≤ ω_n^{−1/2}R₀^{−n/2}(‖w‖_{L²(B̆_{R₀})} + ‖h − w‖_{L²(B̆_{R₀})}) ≤ ω_n^{−1/2}(R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆_{R₀}}w²)^{1/2} + ω_n^{−1/2}R₀^{−n/2}(ε'R₀^{n+2})^{1/2} ≤ C·√(∫_{B̆_{R₀}}w²/R₀ⁿ) + C√ε' R₀.
D3. For θ' ∈ (0, 1/4], by (u + u')² ≤ 2u² + 2u'², Part B and C4: ∫_{B̆_{θ'R₀}}(w − a − b(v))²dv ≤ 2∫_{B̆_{R₀}}(w − h)² + 2∫_{B̆_{θ'R₀}}(h − ℓ)² ≤ 2ε'R₀^{n+2} + 2ω_n(θ'R₀)ⁿ(½C₁θ'²R₀)² = (θ'R₀)^{n+2}(2ε'/θ'^{n+2} + ½ω_nC₁²θ'²) ≤ C(ε'/θ'^{n+2} + θ'²)(θ'R₀)^{n+2}.
D1–D3 are the three asserted conclusions; C does not depend on ε', and δ_h depends only on n and ε'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Harmonic approximation (Simon 3.1) by contradiction, using the Poincaré inequality, Rellich compactness, weak limits and Weyl's lemma.
Scale to radius R₀.
Mean-value and derivative estimates for harmonic h (Simon 3.2–3.4), and Taylor expansion on B_{θ'R₀}.
Set a := h(0) and b := Dh(0), and derive the bounds on ‖b‖, |a| and ∫(w − a − b)².

subproblem.title: Measurability of the approximate tangent projection of an integer multiplicity triple
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (Lean IMRep U n) with weight μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then the map x ↦ p_{T_xM} from ℝ^P to the continuous linear endomorphisms of ℝ^P, where p_{T_xM} is the orthogonal projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x (the approximate tangent plane of M at x when it exists, the zero subspace otherwise), is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ_R.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) R.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this measurability is used implicitly throughout Simon, Ch. 3–5 (the approximate tangent space of a rectifiable set is Hⁿ-measurable, and integrals such as ∫div_M X dμ, ∫|p_x − p_S|²dμ presuppose it); the parent proof uses it whenever it integrates functions of p_x. The proof below derives it from the IMRep fields.

1. Notation and reduction. E := ℝ^P (Lean Euclid P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩; M := R.carrier; ν := Hⁿ⌞M (Lean μHE[n].restrict R.carrier); R.measure = ν.withDensity θ, so R.measure ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). Hence it suffices to show that x ↦ p_{T_xM} := (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection is AE-strongly measurable with respect to ν (then AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac gives the claim for R.measure). For a submodule Q, p_Q := Q.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto Q, an element of the finite-dimensional normed space End(E) := E →L[ℝ] E. The orientation ξ := R.orient takes values in MultiVector P n, the (finite-dimensional) normed space of continuous linear functionals on Covector E n (continuous alternating n-linear forms E^n → ℝ); IsUnitOrientationOf η Q means: there are τ = (τ₁,…,τₙ) orthonormal with span{τ_m} = Q and s ∈ {1, −1} such that η(β) = s·β(τ₁,…,τₙ) for every β ∈ Covector E n. By the IMRep field aestronglyMeasurable_orient, ξ is AE-strongly measurable with respect to ν.

2. Identification of T_xM. By the IMRep field orients there is a ν-null set N₁ such that for every x ∉ N₁ some submodule Q_x satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. For such x the existential condition in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so approxTangentPlane n M x is a submodule Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'; by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); library HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q' = Q_x. Hence p_{T_xM} = p_{Q_x} for every x ∉ N₁.

3. Case n = 0. Every submodule of finrank 0 is ⊥, and approxTangentPlane 0 M x = ⊥ in both branches of its definition (an approximate tangent plane has finrank n = 0). So the map is the constant 0, which is strongly measurable. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.

4. A unit simple n-vector determines its plane. Let η ∈ MultiVector P n satisfy η(β) = s·β(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all β, with τ orthonormal and s = ±1. Claim: span τ = {v ∈ E : η(ι_vγ) = 0 for every γ ∈ Covector E (n+1)}, where ι_vγ ∈ Covector E n is (u₁,…,uₙ) ↦ γ(v, u₁,…,uₙ). If v ∈ span τ then η(ι_vγ) = s·γ(v, τ₁,…,τₙ) = 0, because the n + 1 arguments are linearly dependent and γ is alternating. If v ∉ span τ, let w := v − Σ_i⟨v, τ_i⟩τ_i ≠ 0 (w ⊥ τ_i) and γ(u₀,…,uₙ) := det(⟨c_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b=0..n} with c := (w, τ₁,…,τₙ); γ is a continuous alternating (n+1)-form. The matrix (⟨c_a, u_b⟩) for (u₀,…,uₙ) := (v, τ₁,…,τₙ) has first row (⟨w, v⟩, ⟨w, τ₁⟩,…) = (|w|², 0,…,0) and lower-right n×n block (⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = I_n, so γ(v, τ₁,…,τₙ) = |w|² and η(ι_vγ) = s|w|² ≠ 0. Consequently, if IsUnitOrientationOf η Q and IsUnitOrientationOf η Q', then Q = Q' (both equal the set above).

5. A Borel map Ĝ : MultiVector P n → End(E) with Ĝ(η) = p_Q whenever IsUnitOrientationOf η Q. Let Ω := {(τ, s) : τ ∈ E^n orthonormal, s ∈ {1, −1}}; it is compact (closed and bounded in E^n × ℝ). Ψ(τ, s) := (β ↦ s·β(τ₁,…,τₙ)) defines a continuous map Ω → MultiVector P n (the evaluation pairing (β, τ) ↦ β(τ) is continuous and multilinear, and |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ when |τ_i| = 1). Its image 𝒮 := Ψ(Ω) is compact, hence closed, and equals {η : ∃ Q, IsUnitOrientationOf η Q}. The map G̃(τ, s) := p_{span τ} = Σ_i⟨τ_i, ·⟩τ_i is continuous on Ω, and by 4 it is constant on the fibres of Ψ; hence G̃ = G ∘ Ψ for a unique G : 𝒮 → End(E). Since Ψ : Ω → 𝒮 is a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, it is a closed map, hence a quotient map, so G is continuous on 𝒮. Let Ĝ := G on 𝒮 and Ĝ := 0 off 𝒮; Ĝ is Borel measurable (𝒮 is closed and G is continuous on it), and Ĝ(η) = p_Q whenever IsUnitOrientationOf η Q.

6. Conclusion. ξ is AE-strongly measurable for ν, hence AE-measurable (MultiVector P n is finite dimensional, so second countable with its Borel σ-algebra), and Ĝ is Borel, so Ĝ ∘ ξ is ν-AE-measurable; End(E) is finite dimensional (second countable, metrizable), so Ĝ ∘ ξ is ν-AE-strongly measurable. By 2 and 5, Ĝ(ξ x) = p_{Q_x} = p_{T_xM} for every x ∉ N₁, so x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection agrees ν-a.e. with Ĝ ∘ ξ and is ν-AE-strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr). By 1, it is AE-strongly measurable with respect to R.measure. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to Hⁿ⌞M: R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Hⁿ⌞M (mono_ac).
For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, approxTangentPlane n M x is the plane Q_x oriented by orient x (IMRep.orients and uniqueness of approximate tangent planes).
Case n = 0: the map is identically 0.
A unit simple n-vector determines its plane: span τ = {v : η(ι_vγ) = 0 for all (n+1)-covectors γ}, via the determinant form γ = det(⟨c_a, ·⟩).
The compact set Ω of orthonormal frames maps onto the closed set 𝒮 of unit simple n-vectors by a quotient map, so η ↦ p_Q is continuous on 𝒮; extending by 0 gives a Borel map Ĝ.
Ĝ ∘ orient is AE-strongly measurable and agrees a.e. with x ↦ p_{T_xM}.

subproblem.title: Monotonicity inequalities and unit density lower bound for bounded mean curvature
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), W ⊆ U open, κ ∈ ℝ, H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x, such that R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} with tsupport X ⊆ W. For y ∈ ℝ^{n+k} let F_y(x) := |p_x^⊥(x − y)|²/|x − y|^{n+2} (0 at x = y). Then (1) for every y and 0 < s < t with B_t(y) ⊆ W: (M1) ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} F_y dμ + e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) and (M2) e^{−κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{−κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) + ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} F_y dμ; and (2) for every y ∈ spt μ and t > 0 with B_t(y) ⊆ W: (D) ∫_{B_t(y)} F_y dμ + ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)), where ω_n = unitBallVolume n. Here p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x^⊥ := I − p_x, p_S the orthogonal projection onto a subspace S, |A|² := Σ_i |Ae_i|² the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (the Lean sum over EuclideanSpace.single i 1), B_t(y) the closed ball, and integrals of nonnegative functions are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞] (Lean ∫⁻ of ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (U W : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (R : IMRep U n) (H : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k)) (κ : ℝ), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable H R.measure → (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) → (∀ X : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k), ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ W → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) → (∀ (y : Euclid (n + k)) (s t : ℝ), 0 < s → s < t → closedBall y t ⊆ W → (∫⁻ x in closedBall y t \ closedBall y s, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - y) - (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ (n + 2)) ∂R.measure) + ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ * s) / s ^ n) * R.measure (closedBall y s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ * t) / t ^ n) * R.measure (closedBall y t) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(κ * t)) / t ^ n) * R.measure (closedBall y t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(κ * s)) / s ^ n) * R.measure (closedBall y s) + ∫⁻ x in closedBall y t \ closedBall y s, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - y) - (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ (n + 2)) ∂R.measure) ∧ ∀ y ∈ R.measure.support, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → closedBall y t ⊆ W → (∫⁻ x in closedBall y t, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - y) - (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ (n + 2)) ∂R.measure) + unitBallVolume n ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ * t) / t ^ n) * R.measure (closedBall y t)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Sibling map (dependency key — frozen Lean declaration — labels used below): tangent_projection_measurable — Submission.dorag_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (x ↦ p_x is AE-strongly measurable for μ = R.measure).
Source: parent proof Part 1.1–1.3 (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2–3.6, 3.16–3.17 with bounded H, and 4.10(1); Ch. 3, 1.5(3)). Conventions: E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(y) closed ball, B̆_t(y) open ball; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, Hⁿ := μHE[n], ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); p_x := projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x^⊥ := I − p_x. Write F_y(x) := |p_x^⊥(x − y)|²/|x − y|^{n+2} (the integrand; F_y(y) = 0 by the convention 0/0 = 0). All integrals of nonnegative functions are in [0, ∞].
Preliminaries. (P1) κ ≥ 0 since κ ≥ ‖H(x)‖. (P2) For compact K ⊆ W, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ by IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult (K ⊆ W ⊆ U); if B_t(y) ⊆ W then, W being open and B_t(y) compact, B_{R'}(y) ⊆ W for some R' > t. (P3) For μ-a.e. x: x ∈ M, T_xM is an n-dimensional approximate tangent plane of M at x (IMRep.orients, definition of approxTangentPlane, uniqueness HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so trace p_x = n; x ↦ p_x is μ-measurable (sibling tangent_projection_measurable), hence F_y is μ-measurable. (P4) For C¹ compactly supported X with tsupport X ⊆ W, div_M X(x) = trace(p_x∘DX(x)) is bounded, measurable and compactly supported in W, so R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ, and (MC) reads ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ. (P5) μ({y}) = θ(y)Hⁿ({y}) = 0 for every y, since n ≥ 1.

(Remark: the library's Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean proves the analogous cutoff identity HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.cutoffMass_deriv_identity and monotonicity HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn for its own varifold structure; they can serve as templates, but they do not contain the annular term ∫F_y dμ, so (M1), (M2) are proved here.)
Step 1 (the identity). Fix y and 0 < s < t with B_t(y) ⊆ W, and R' > t with B_{R'}(y) ⊆ W (P2). Let r(x) := |x − y|, and for x ≠ y let ∇r := (x − y)/r and D^⊥r(x) := p_x^⊥(∇r), so |D^⊥r|² ≤ 1 and r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² = F_y. Fix ε' ∈ (0, 1) with (1 + ε')t < R', and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ' ≤ 0, φ ≡ 1 on (−∞, 1], φ ≡ 0 on [1 + ε', ∞). For τ ∈ (0, R'/(1+ε')) let X_τ(x) := φ(r/τ)(x − y). X_τ is C¹ (it equals x − y on B̆_τ(y), and away from y it is a composition of C¹ maps), compactly supported, with tsupport X_τ ⊆ B_{(1+ε')τ}(y) ⊆ W. At x ≠ y, DX_τ(x) = φ(r/τ)I + τ^{−1}φ'(r/τ)(x − y)⊗∇r (i.e. h ↦ φ(r/τ)h + τ^{−1}φ'(r/τ)⟨∇r, h⟩(x − y)); hence at μ-a.e. x (P3, P5), div_M X_τ(x) = nφ(r/τ) + τ^{−1}φ'(r/τ)⟨p_x(x − y), ∇r⟩ = nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²), because ⟨p_x∇r, ∇r⟩ = |p_x∇r|² = 1 − |D^⊥r|².
 Put I(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)dμ, J(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)|D^⊥r|²dμ and h(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ. All integrands vanish outside B_{R'}(y), which has finite μ-measure (P2); ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)] = −(r/τ²)φ'(r/τ) ≥ 0 is bounded by sup|φ'|(1+ε')/τ, uniformly for τ in compact subintervals; so by differentiation under the integral sign I and J are C¹ with I'(τ) = ∫∂_τ[φ(r/τ)]dμ and J'(τ) = ∫∂_τ[φ(r/τ)]|D^⊥r|²dμ ≥ 0. Since (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) = −τ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)], (MC) applied to X_τ (P4) gives nI(τ) − τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ) = −h(τ). As φ(r/τ) ≠ 0 only where r ≤ (1+ε')τ, |h(τ)| ≤ (1+ε')κτ I(τ).
Step 2 (integration). Let g(τ) := τ^{−n}I(τ) and c := (1+ε')κ ≥ 0. From Step 1, g' = τ^{−n−1}(τI' − nI) = τ^{−n}J' + e with e := τ^{−n−1}h, |e| ≤ cg. Hence (e^{cτ}g)' = e^{cτ}(τ^{−n}J' + e + cg) ≥ e^{cτ}τ^{−n}J' ≥ τ^{−n}J' and (e^{−cτ}g)' = e^{−cτ}(τ^{−n}J' + e − cg) ≤ e^{−cτ}τ^{−n}J' ≤ τ^{−n}J' (J' ≥ 0, c ≥ 0). Integrating over [s, t]:
 (i) ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J'(τ)dτ ≤ e^{ct}g(t) − e^{cs}g(s);  (ii) e^{−ct}g(t) − e^{−cs}g(s) ≤ ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J'(τ)dτ.
 By Tonelli (nonnegative integrand), ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J'(τ)dτ = ∫|D^⊥r|²Λ dμ with Λ(x) := ∫_s^t τ^{−n}∂_τ[φ(r/τ)]dτ. Since ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)] ≥ 0 vanishes unless r/(1+ε') ≤ τ ≤ r, where r^{−n} ≤ τ^{−n} ≤ (1+ε')ⁿr^{−n}, and ∫_s^t∂_τ[φ(r/τ)]dτ = φ(r/t) − φ(r/s), we have r^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)) ≤ Λ ≤ (1+ε')ⁿr^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)). Moreover 1_{B_t(y)∖B_{(1+ε')s}(y)} ≤ φ(r/t) − φ(r/s) ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε')t}(y)∖B_s(y)} and μ(B_τ(y)) ≤ I(τ) ≤ μ(B_{(1+ε')τ}(y)). Therefore (i) gives
 (i') ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_{(1+ε')s}(y)} F_y dμ + e^{cs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ e^{ct}t^{−n}μ(B_{(1+ε')t}(y)),
 and (ii) gives
 (ii') e^{−ct}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{−cs}s^{−n}μ(B_{(1+ε')s}(y)) + (1+ε')ⁿ∫_{B_{(1+ε')t}(y)∖B_s(y)} F_y dμ.
Step 3 (limit ε' ↓ 0; (M1), (M2)). Let ε' ↓ 0 along a sequence. Then c → κ; μ(B_{(1+ε')τ}(y)) ↓ μ(B_τ(y)) for τ ∈ {s, t} (closed balls decreasing to the closed ball, finite measure); the sets B_t(y)∖B_{(1+ε')s}(y) increase to B_t(y)∖B_s(y), so the first integral in (i') increases to ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ (monotone convergence); and the sets B_{(1+ε')t}(y)∖B_s(y) decrease to B_t(y)∖B_s(y) with F_y ≤ s^{−n} on them and finite measure, so the integral in (ii') converges to ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ. All quantities are finite, so in [0, ∞]: (M1) ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ + e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)); (M2) e^{−κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{−κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) + ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ. This is the first conclusion (in Lean: ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ s)/sⁿ) * μ(B_s(y)) etc.).
Step 4 (monotonicity and density). By (M1) (its integral term is ≥ 0), for y with B_{t₀}(y) ⊆ W the function τ ↦ e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_τ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, t₀]. Hence for y ∈ W the limit Θ(μ, y) := lim_{τ↓0} μ(B_τ(y))/(ω_nτⁿ) exists in [0, ∞) (e^{κτ} → 1).
Step 5 (Θ ≥ 1 on spt μ ∩ W; Simon Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). (i) Let x ∈ M ∩ W be a point where M has an approximate tangent plane Q (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, dim Q = n). For ε'' ∈ (0, 1) choose continuous compactly supported ψ₋ ≤ ψ₊ with 1_{B_{1−ε''}(0)} ≤ ψ₋ ≤ 1_{B_1(0)} ≤ ψ₊ ≤ 1_{B_{1+ε''}(0)}. With η_{x,λ}(y') := λ^{−1}(y' − x) one has Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(M) ∩ B_ρ'(0)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λρ'}(x)) (scaling of Hⁿ), so λ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λ(1−ε'')}(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)}ψ₋dHⁿ and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)}ψ₊dHⁿ ≤ λ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λ(1+ε'')}(x)) (for λ so small that B_{2λ}(x) ⊆ W, Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{2λ}(x)) ≤ μ(B_{2λ}(x)) < ∞ by (P2) and θ ≥ 1 on M, so ψ_± are integrable for Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(M) and these Bochner integrals, which are the ones in the library definition of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt, are genuine integrals); by the definition of approximate tangent plane these integrals converge to ∫_Qψ_± dHⁿ ∈ [ω_n(1−ε'')ⁿ, ω_n(1+ε'')ⁿ] (Hⁿ⌞Q is Lebesgue measure on the n-plane Q). Letting ε'' ↓ 0: Hⁿ(M ∩ B_λ(x))/(ω_nλⁿ) → 1 as λ ↓ 0 (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(3)). Since μ ≥ Hⁿ⌞M (θ ≥ 1 on M), Θ(μ, x) ≥ 1. By (P3) this holds for μ-a.e. x ∈ W.
 (ii) Θ(μ, ·) is upper semicontinuous on W: let y_j → y ∈ W, and τ, ε'' > 0 with B_{τ+ε''}(y) ⊆ W. For large j, |y_j − y| ≤ ε'', so B_τ(y_j) ⊆ B_{τ+ε''}(y) ⊆ W and by Step 4 at y_j, Θ(μ, y_j) ≤ ω_n^{−1}e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_τ(y_j)) ≤ ω_n^{−1}e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_{τ+ε''}(y)). Let j → ∞, then ε'' ↓ 0 (μ(B_{τ+ε''}(y)) ↓ μ(B_τ(y))), then τ ↓ 0: limsup_j Θ(μ, y_j) ≤ Θ(μ, y).
 (iii) Let y ∈ spt μ ∩ W. For large j the open ball B̆_{1/j}(y) lies in W and has positive μ-measure (definition of support), so by (i) it contains a point x_j with Θ(μ, x_j) ≥ 1. As x_j → y, (ii) gives Θ(μ, y) ≥ 1.
Step 6 ((D)). Let y ∈ spt μ and t > 0 with B_t(y) ⊆ W (so y ∈ W). For 0 < s < t, (M1) gives ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ + e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)). Let s ↓ 0 along a sequence: the sets B_t(y)∖B_s(y) increase to B_t(y)∖{y}, and μ({y}) = 0 (P5), so the integrals increase to ∫_{B_t(y)}F_y dμ (monotone convergence); and e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) → ω_nΘ(μ, y) ≥ ω_n by Steps 4–5. Hence for every c < ω_n, ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)}F_y dμ + c ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) for all small s, and letting s ↓ 0 and then c ↑ ω_n: ∫_{B_t(y)}F_y dμ + ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)). This is the second conclusion. ∎

The first variation identity yields nI − τI' + τJ' = −h with |h| ≤ (1+ε')κτI, hence (e^{cτ}g)' ≥ τ^{−n}J' and (e^{−cτ}g)' ≤ τ^{−n}J' for g = τ^{−n}I.
Integrate over [s, t], use Tonelli and the cutoff bounds, then let ε' ↓ 0 to obtain (M1) and (M2) with closed balls.
(M1) gives monotonicity of e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_τ(y)), so Θ(μ, y) exists.
Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e. via the density of M at approximate tangent points, upper semicontinuity of Θ, hence Θ ≥ 1 on spt μ ∩ W.
Let s ↓ 0 in (M1) to obtain (D).

subproblem.title: The support minus the carrier is Hⁿ-null
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), W ⊆ U open, κ ∈ ℝ, H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x, such that R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} with tsupport X ⊆ W. Then Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n].

Sibling map (dependency key — frozen Lean declaration — labels used below): monotonicity — Submission.dorag_monotonicity_density ((M1) and (M2) are the first and second conjuncts of its first conclusion ∀ y s t, 0 < s → s < t → closedBall y t ⊆ W → (M1) ∧ (M2); (D) is its second conclusion ∀ y ∈ spt μ, ∀ t > 0, closedBall y t ⊆ W → ∫_{B_t(y)}F_y dμ + ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y))).
Source: parent proof Part 1.4 (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3 comparison theorem; Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). Conventions: E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(x) closed ball; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞). Sibling used: monotonicity (statement (D)).

1. Let A' := (spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M. Since μ = θHⁿ⌞M is concentrated on M, μ(A') ≤ μ(E ∖ M) = 0.
2. Density lower bound on A'. Let x ∈ A' ⊆ spt μ ∩ W. Since W is open there is t₀ > 0 with B_{t₀}(x) ⊆ W, and then B_t(x) ⊆ W for all t ∈ (0, t₀]. By the sibling monotonicity (conclusion (D), whose integral term is ≥ 0), ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)), i.e. μ(B_t(x)) ≥ e^{−κt}ω_ntⁿ for t ∈ (0, t₀]. Hence limsup_{t↓0} μ(B_t(x))/(ω_ntⁿ) ≥ 1 (indeed liminf ≥ lim e^{−κt} = 1).
3. Small open neighbourhood of A'. Let ε'' > 0. For j ≥ 1 let V_j := {x ∈ W : |x| < j, dist(x, E ∖ W) > 1/j} (V_j := {|x| < j} if W = E). Each V_j is open, its closure is a compact subset of W, so μ(V_j) < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult, as W ⊆ U), and ∪_j V_j = W. The finite Borel measure μ⌞V_j on E is outer regular and (μ⌞V_j)(A' ∩ V_j) = 0, so there is an open O_j ⊇ A' ∩ V_j with μ(O_j ∩ V_j) < ε''2^{−j}. Put O := ∪_j (O_j ∩ V_j): O is open, A' ⊆ O ⊆ W and μ(O) < ε''.
4. Comparison. For x ∈ A' ⊆ O, B_t(x) ⊆ O for small t (O open), so the upper n-density of the measure μ⌞O at x, limsup_{t↓0} μ(O ∩ B_t(x))/(ω_ntⁿ), equals limsup_{t↓0} μ(B_t(x))/(ω_ntⁿ) ≥ 1 by 2. By (D), the upper n-density of μ is ≥ 1 at every point of A'.
Choose an open O with A' ⊆ O ⊆ W and μ(O) < ε'' (outer regularity on compactly contained pieces of W).
The density comparison theorem gives Hⁿ(A') ≤ μ(O) < ε''; let ε'' ↓ 0.

subproblem.statement: For n ≥ 1 and k ≥ 0 there are θ₀ ∈ (0, 1/4] and δ₂ ∈ (0, 1/8] such that for every δ ∈ (0, δ₂] and all data satisfying (SA_δ): U, W ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} with W open and W ⊆ U; R = (M, θ, ξ_R) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n; ξ_R = R.orient is its orientation, and ξ below denotes a point) with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M; H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x; R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X with tsupport X ⊆ W; ρ > 0 with the closed ball B_ρ(z) ⊆ W; z ∈ spt μ; μ(B_ρ(z)) ≤ (1 + δ)ω_nρⁿ (ω_n = unitBallVolume n); κρ ≤ δ: for every ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{δρ}(z), σ ∈ (0, δρ] and n-dimensional subspace T there is an n-dimensional subspace S with E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T), where E_*(ξ, r, S') := max{r^{−n}∫_{B_r(ξ)} |p_x − p_{S'}|² dμ, κ²r²/δ} ∈ [0, ∞]. Here p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, p_S the orthogonal projection onto a subspace S, |A|² := Σ_i |Ae_i|² the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (the Lean sum over EuclideanSpace.single i 1), B_t(y) the closed ball, and integrals of nonnegative functions are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞] (Lean ∫⁻ of ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → ∃ θ₀ δ₂ : ℝ, 0 < θ₀ ∧ θ₀ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ 0 < δ₂ ∧ δ₂ ≤ 1 / 8 ∧ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₂ → ∀ (U W : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (R : IMRep U n) (H : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k)) (κ ρ : ℝ) (z : Euclid (n + k)), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → 0 < ρ → closedBall z ρ ⊆ W → AEStronglyMeasurable H R.measure → (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) → (∀ X : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k), ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ W → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) → z ∈ R.measure.support → R.measure (closedBall z ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (1 + δ) * unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) → κ * ρ ≤ δ → ∀ ξ ∈ R.measure.support ∩ closedBall z (δ * ρ), ∀ (σ : ℝ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid (n + k))), 0 < σ → σ ≤ δ * ρ → Module.finrank ℝ T = n → ∃ S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid (n + k)), Module.finrank ℝ S = n ∧ max (ENNReal.ofReal (1 / (θ₀ * σ) ^ n) * ∫⁻ x in closedBall ξ (θ₀ * σ), ENNReal.ofReal (∑ i : Fin (n + k), ‖(approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) - S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure) (ENNReal.ofReal (κ ^ 2 * (θ₀ * σ) ^ 2 / δ)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal θ₀ * max (ENNReal.ofReal (1 / σ ^ n) * ∫⁻ x in closedBall ξ σ, ENNReal.ofReal (∑ i : Fin (n + k), ‖(approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) - T.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure) (ENNReal.ofReal (κ ^ 2 * σ ^ 2 / δ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Sibling map (dependency key — frozen Lean declaration — labels used below): tangent_projection_measurable — Submission.dorag_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (x ↦ p_x is AE-strongly measurable for μ = R.measure); support_null — Submission.dorag_support_sdiff_carrier_null (Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0); graph_tangent — Submission.dorag_lipschitz_graph_approxTangent (tangent planes along a Lipschitz graph); tilt_height — Submission.dorag_tilt_height_estimate (constant C_T for the given n, k); harmonic_approximation — Submission.dorag_harmonic_affine_approximation (constant C_H; δ_h(ε') for each ε' > 0); density_bounds — Submission.dorag_standing_density_bounds (constants δ₁, C₂; (a), (b), (c), (d) are its four conclusions in order); affine_approximation — Submission.dorag_affine_approximation (constants δ₃, C₃; (4a) is its distance bound, (4b) its integral bound); lipschitz_approximation — Submission.dorag_lipschitz_approximation (constants δ₅, β, β', C₇ for the given C₆; 5A is the conjunction before its final implication, 5B is the final implication).
Source: parent proof Part 7, Claim 7A and its proof, Steps 1–10 (Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 4.5 with p = 2n, bounded H, and the corrections recorded there). Conventions: E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(y) closed ball, B̆_t(y) open ball, Bⁿ_t, B̆ⁿ_t balls of ℝⁿ about 0; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); p_x := projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x; |A|² Hilbert–Schmidt (the Lean sums), ‖A‖ ≤ |A|; E(ξ, r, S) := r^{−n}∫_{B_r(ξ)}|p_x − p_S|²dμ; α := 1/(2n+2); E_*(ξ, r, S) := max{E(ξ, r, S), δ^{−1}κ²r²} (the Lean max of ofReal(1/rⁿ)·∫⁻ and ofReal(κ²r²/δ)). "C" denotes constants depending only on n, k. Siblings used: density_bounds ((a), (b), (d); constant δ₁), affine_approximation (δ₃, C₃), lipschitz_approximation (applied with C₆ := C₁₁ below; δ₅, β, C₇), tilt_height (C_T), harmonic_approximation (C_H, δ_h(ε')), graph_tangent, support_null, tangent_projection_measurable.

Preliminaries. (P1) κ ≥ 0 since κ ≥ ‖H(x)‖. (P2) For compact K ⊆ W, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult, K ⊆ W ⊆ U) and Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) (θ ≥ 1 on M); if B_t(y) ⊆ W then B_{t'}(y) ⊆ W for some t' > t. (P3) For μ-a.e. x: x ∈ M and T_xM is an n-dimensional approximate tangent plane of M at x (IMRep.orients, the definition of approxTangentPlane and uniqueness HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-plane and trace p_x = n; x ↦ p_x is μ-AE-strongly measurable (tangent_projection_measurable). (P4) (MC) denotes the hypothesis R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X with tsupport X ⊆ W; for such X, div_M X(x) = trace(p_x∘DX(x)) (Lean tangentialDivergence) is bounded, μ-measurable (P3) and supported in a compact subset of W, hence μ-integrable (P2), and R.firstVariation X = ∫_Mθ div_M X dHⁿ = ∫div_M X dμ; so (MC) reads ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ. (P5) μ(E ∖ M) = 0 and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0; μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M and Hⁿ⌞M ≤ μ, so μ-null and Hⁿ⌞M-null sets coincide.
0. Constants. Let C₁₁ := 2C₃ + (8C₃/ω_n)^{1/2} and take δ₅, β, β', C₇ from lipschitz_approximation with C₆ := C₁₁ (≥ C₃ ≥ 1). The constants C₁₂,…,C₁₆ introduced in Steps 6–9 depend only on n, k (through the sibling constants; none depends on θ', ε' or δ). θ', ε', θ₀ := θ'/32 and δ₂ are fixed in Step 10, in this order; θ₀ and δ₂ are the constants asserted to exist.
Claim (the asserted statement): for 0 < δ ≤ δ₂ under the hypotheses, every ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{r₁}(z) (r₁ := δρ), σ ∈ (0, r₁] and n-plane T admit an n-plane S with E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T). Fix such δ, data, ξ, σ and T; Steps 1–10 construct S.
1. Reduction (Simon (1)–(2)). All points used lie in B_{4r₁}(z) and all radii are ≤ 2σ ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ, so density_bounds applies; κ ≥ 0 and κρ ≤ δ. affine_approximation at (ξ, 2σ) (ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{2r₁}(z), 2σ ≤ 2r₁) gives an n-plane T̃ with E(ξ, σ, T̃) ≤ C₃δ^{2α} and dist(x − ξ, T̃) ≤ 2C₃δ^ασ for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{2σ}(ξ). If E(ξ, σ, T) > C₃δ^{2α} then E_*(ξ, σ, T̃) ≤ E_*(ξ, σ, T), and an S with E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T̃) also works for T; so we may assume E(ξ, σ, T) ≤ C₃δ^{2α}. Then |p_T − p_{T̃}|²μ(B_σ(ξ)) ≤ 2∫_{B_σ(ξ)}|p_x − p_T|² + 2∫_{B_σ(ξ)}|p_x − p_{T̃}|² ≤ 4C₃δ^{2α}σⁿ and μ(B_σ(ξ)) ≥ ½ω_nσⁿ (density_bounds (b)), so ‖p_T − p_{T̃}‖ ≤ (8C₃/ω_n)^{1/2}δ^α and
 (2') dist(x − ξ, T) ≤ dist(x − ξ, T̃) + ‖p_T − p_{T̃}‖|x − ξ| ≤ C₁₁δ^ασ for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_σ(ξ).
 Let E₀ := E_*(ξ, σ, T). Since κσ ≤ κr₁ ≤ δ², δ^{−1}κ²σ² ≤ δ³ ≤ C₃δ^{2α}; so E₀ ≤ C₃δ^{2α} (δ ≤ 1, C₃ ≥ 1). If E₀ = 0 then E(ξ, σ, T) = 0 and κ = 0, and S := T works because E(ξ, θ₀σ, T) ≤ θ₀^{−n}E(ξ, σ, T) = 0. Assume E₀ > 0.
2. Lipschitz approximation (Simon (3)–(4)). Require δ^α ≤ β (Step 10). lipschitz_approximation at (ξ, σ₀ := σ, T₀ := T, L := 1, C₆ := C₁₁) — hypotheses (i) E(ξ, σ, T) ≤ C₃δ^{2α} ≤ C₁₁δ^{2α} and (ii) = (2') — gives linear isometries ι : ℝⁿ → E, ι' : ℝᵏ → E with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 and ι(ℝⁿ) ⊆ T (hence ι(ℝⁿ) = T, ι'(ℝᵏ) = T^⊥ by dimensions), and f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with Lip f ≤ 1, |f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ, and with Φ_f(v) := ξ + ιv + ι'f(v), F := Φ_f(ℝⁿ):
 (4') μ(B_{σ/2}(ξ) ∖ F) + Hⁿ((F ∖ spt μ) ∩ B_{σ/4}(ξ)) ≤ C₇∫_{B_σ(ξ)}|p_x − p_T|²dμ ≤ C₇σⁿE₀.
 Coordinates: for x ∈ E write x − ξ = ιx' + ι'x'' with x' := ι*(x − ξ) ∈ ℝⁿ, x'' := ι'*(x − ξ) ∈ ℝᵏ; |x''| = dist(x − ξ, T); e_{n+j} := ι'(ε_j) (ε_j standard basis of ℝᵏ), fʲ := ⟨f, ε_j⟩, ∇fʲ its a.e. gradient (Rademacher), Df the a.e. derivative of f. Put r := σ/4 and R₀ := r/2 = σ/8. (Correction: Simon works on B_σ; since (4') controls F ∖ spt μ only on B_{σ/4}, the harmonic approximation is done on Bⁿ_{σ/8}.)
3. Height (Simon (5)). Require C₁₁δ^α ≤ 1/16 and C₇δ^α ≤ 1/16. Then x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_σ(ξ) with |x'| < r/2 has |x''| ≤ r/4, hence |x − ξ| < 3r/4; and |Φ_f(v) − ξ| ≤ |v| + |f(v)| < 3r/4 for |v| < r/2.
4. Equation for fʲ (Simon (6)–(9)). Fix j and ζ ∈ C¹_c(B̆_r(ξ)). X := ζe_{n+j} is C¹ with compact support in B_r(ξ) ⊆ B_ρ(z) ⊆ W and div_M X = ⟨p_xe_{n+j}, ∇ζ⟩ μ-a.e.; (MC) gives (6) ∫⟨p_xe_{n+j}, ∇ζ⟩dμ = −∫ζ⟨e_{n+j}, H⟩dμ. Let M₁ := M ∩ F. By graph_tangent (with a := ξ, L := 1; Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ W, hence μ-a.e. on W), for μ-a.e. x = Φ_f(v) ∈ M₁ ∩ B_r(ξ), f is differentiable at v and T_xM = {ιw + ι'Df(v)w}; for τ' = ιw + ι'Df(v)w ∈ T_xM, ⟨τ', e_{n+j}⟩ = ⟨Df(v)w, ε_j⟩ = ⟨w, ∇fʲ(v)⟩ = ⟨τ', ι∇fʲ(v)⟩, so (7) p_xe_{n+j} = p_x ι∇fʲ(v) =: ∇^Mf̃ʲ(x). Hence ∫_{M₁}⟨∇^Mf̃ʲ, ∇ζ⟩dμ = −∫_{M∖M₁}⟨p_xe_{n+j}, ∇ζ⟩dμ − ∫ζ⟨e_{n+j}, H⟩dμ. Write ‖g‖_μ := sup_{spt μ}|g| (only values on spt μ matter, as μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0). Using μ(B_r(ξ) ∖ F) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ (4'), μ(B_r(ξ)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ (density_bounds (a)), |H| ≤ κ, κr ≤ κσ ≤ (δE₀)^{1/2} (as δ^{−1}κ²σ² ≤ E₀) and σⁿ = 4ⁿrⁿ:
 (8') |r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}⟨∇^Mf̃ʲ, ∇ζ⟩dμ| ≤ C(‖∇ζ‖_μE₀ + r^{−1}‖ζ‖_μδ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}); in particular, since ‖ζ‖_μ ≤ sup|ζ| ≤ r sup|∇ζ|, it is ≤ C sup|∇ζ|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀).
 Also |∇^Mf̃ʲ| = |p_xe_{n+j}| = |(p_x − p_T)e_{n+j}| ≤ |p_x − p_T| (p_Te_{n+j} = 0), so (9') r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}|∇^Mf̃ʲ|²dμ ≤ 4ⁿE(ξ, σ, T) ≤ 4ⁿE₀.
5. Tests independent of x'' (Simon (10)–(13)). Let ζ₀ ∈ C¹_c(B̆ⁿ_{r/2}), ζ̃₀(x) := ζ₀(x'), and h₀ ∈ C¹_c(B̆_r(ξ)) with h₀ ≡ 1 on B_{7r/8}(ξ); ζ := ζ̃₀h₀ ∈ C¹_c(B̆_r(ξ)). At x ∈ spt μ: if x ∈ B_σ(ξ) and |x'| < r/2 then x ∈ B̆_{3r/4}(ξ) (Step 3) and ζ = ζ̃₀ near x; if x ∈ B_σ(ξ) and |x'| ≥ r/2 then ζ̃₀ and ζ vanish near x (spt ζ₀ is a compact subset of B̆ⁿ_{r/2}); if x ∉ B_σ(ξ), ζ vanishes near x. Hence ∇ζ = ∇ζ̃₀ = ι∇ζ₀(x') and |ζ| = |ζ̃₀| at every point of spt μ ∩ B_σ(ξ) ⊇ spt μ ∩ B_r(ξ), while ζ = 0 on spt μ ∖ B_σ(ξ); so ‖∇ζ‖_μ ≤ sup|∇ζ₀| and ‖ζ‖_μ ≤ sup|ζ₀| ≤ (r/2)sup|∇ζ₀| (ζ₀ vanishes outside B̆ⁿ_{r/2}). By the first form of (8') applied to ζ, and as μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0: |r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}⟨∇^Mf̃ʲ, ∇ζ̃₀⟩dμ| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀). At μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁, with a := ι∇fʲ(x') and b := ι∇ζ₀(x') in T: ⟨∇^Mf̃ʲ, ∇ζ̃₀⟩ = ⟨p_xa, b⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩ − ⟨p_Tp_x^⊥p_Ta, b⟩, and p_Tp_x^⊥p_T = (p_T − p_x)p_x^⊥(p_T − p_x), so (11) |⟨∇^Mf̃ʲ, ∇ζ̃₀⟩ − ∇fʲ(x')·∇ζ₀(x')| ≤ |p_x − p_T|²|∇fʲ(x')||∇ζ₀(x')|. With |∇fʲ| ≤ 1 and E(ξ, σ, T) ≤ E₀: (12') |r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}∇fʲ(x')·∇ζ₀(x')dμ| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀). Applying (11) with b := a and (9'): (13') r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}|∇fʲ(x')|²dμ ≤ CE₀.
6. Transfer to ℝⁿ (Simon (14)–(16)). Let J_f(v) := (det(I + Df(v)ᵀDf(v)))^{1/2} ∈ [1, 2^{n/2}], so |J_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|², and θ_F(v) := θ(Φ_f(v)) if Φ_f(v) ∈ M, θ_F(v) := 0 otherwise. Since Φ_f is injective and Lipschitz, the area formula (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5; library injective_area_formula_lipschitz) and Step 3 give, for Borel g on ℝⁿ supported in B̆ⁿ_{r/2} and nonnegative or integrable: ∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)}g(x')dμ = ∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}}g(v)θ_F(v)J_f(v)dv (x' = v for x = Φ_f(v)). Let Z₀ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2} : Φ_f(v) ∉ M} and Z₂ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2} : θ_F(v) ≥ 2}. Since |v − v'| ≤ |Φ_f(v) − Φ_f(v')|, Lⁿ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ_f(Z)); Φ_f(Z₀) ⊆ ((F ∖ spt μ) ∩ B_r(ξ)) ∪ ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M), so by (4') and support_null, Lⁿ(Z₀) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ = C₇4ⁿrⁿE₀; Φ_f(Z₂) ⊆ {x ∈ M ∩ B_r(ξ) : θ(x) ≥ 2}, which is μ-null by density_bounds (d) and hence Hⁿ-null, so Lⁿ(Z₂) = 0. Off Z₀ ∪ Z₂, θ_F = 1. Hence from (12'), (13'):
 (16') r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}}|∇fʲ|²dv ≤ CE₀,
 (15') |r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}}∇fʲ·∇ζ₀dv| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀) ≤ C₁₂δ^αE₀^{1/2}sup|∇ζ₀|,
 using ∫_{Z₀}|∇fʲ||∇ζ₀| ≤ sup|∇ζ₀|Lⁿ(Z₀), |θ_FJ_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|² off Z₀ ∪ Z₂ together with (16') summed over j, E₀ ≤ (C₃δ^{2α})^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} and δ^{1/2} ≤ δ^α. (Correction: Simon's factor δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} in (15) becomes δ^{1/(2n+2)}E₀^{1/2}, which suffices.)
7. Harmonic approximation (Simon (17)). By (16') choose C₁₃ with R₀^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{R₀}}|∇fʲ|² ≤ C₁₃E₀ for all j. Then w := (C₁₃E₀)^{−1/2}fʲ is Lipschitz, satisfies ∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}}|∇w|² ≤ R₀ⁿ and, by (15') with r = 2R₀, |∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}}∇w·∇ζ₀| ≤ C₁₄δ^αR₀ⁿ G for ζ₀ ∈ C¹_c with tsupport in B̆ⁿ_{R₀} and |∇ζ₀| ≤ G, where C₁₄ := 2ⁿC₁₂C₁₃^{−1/2}. Require C₁₄δ^α ≤ δ_h(n, ε') (Step 10). harmonic_approximation gives a_j ∈ ℝ and a linear b_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ‖b_j‖ ≤ C_H, |a_j| ≤ C_H(R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}}w²)^{1/2} + C_H√ε'R₀, and ∫_{B̆ⁿ_{θ'R₀}}(w − a_j − b_j)² ≤ C_H(ε'θ'^{−n−2} + θ'²)(θ'R₀)^{n+2} for θ' ∈ (0, 1/4]. Let λ := (λ¹,…,λᵏ), λʲ(v) := (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}(a_j + b_j(v)), u(0) := λ(0), Du(0) := Dλ (in the parent's notation λ(v) = u(0) + Du(0)v).
8. Affine approximation of f (Simon (18)–(19)). From 7: |Du(0)| ≤ CE₀^{1/2}; since |f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ = 8C₇δ^αR₀ and E₀ ≤ C₃δ^{2α}, ε' ≤ 1: (18') |u(0)| ≤ C₁₅R₀δ^α; and for θ' ∈ (0, 1/4] (summing over j): (19') (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}}|f − λ|²dv ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'²)E₀.
9. The new plane (Simon (20)–(22)). Let S := {ιw + ι'Du(0)w : w ∈ ℝⁿ} (an n-plane) and τ := ξ + ι'u(0). Require C₁₅δ^α ≤ θ'/4; then |τ − ξ| ≤ θ'R₀/4 and B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ B_{σ/2}(ξ). For x = Φ_f(v) with |v| ≤ θ'R₀, dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |f(v) − λ(v)|, and F ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ Φ_f(Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}) (|v| = |x' − τ'| ≤ |x − τ|, τ' = 0). Split ∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)}dist(x − τ, S)²dμ into the parts on F and off F. On F, μ⌞F ≤ Hⁿ⌞F on B_{4r₁}(z) (θ = 1 μ-a.e. there by density_bounds (d), μ = θHⁿ⌞M), and the area formula with J_f ≤ 2^{n/2} bounds it by 2^{n/2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}}|f − λ|². Off F, each x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) has dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |x''| + |u(0)| + |Du(0)||x'| ≤ Cδ^ασ by (2'), (18') and E₀^{1/2} ≤ Cδ^α, and μ(B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ∖ F) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ by (4'). With σ = 8R₀: (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)}dist(x − τ, S)²dμ ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'^{−n−2}δ^{2α} + θ'²)E₀.
